title: To-do on mobile: separate Schedule / Delete row
summary: On phones each task now has its own action row — a Schedule chip on the left and a clearly labelled red Delete button on the far right — so deleting no longer accidentally opens the date picker.
bullets: iOS gives the invisible date-picker control an oversized touch area that was swallowing taps meant for the trash icon; the two actions are now on their own row, far apart.
The Schedule chip shows the booked date right on it, with an ✕ to unschedule.
Desktop keeps the compact inline icons exactly as before.

title: Mobile fixes: header layout + reachable delete
summary: On phones the landing header now wraps cleanly instead of squeezing the To-do/New Page buttons, and the floating back button no longer covers the delete buttons at the bottom of the to-do list.
bullets: The Document Hub title and its buttons wrap onto two rows on narrow screens.
Extra bottom space in the To-do list so every row can scroll clear of the floating back button.
Bigger tap targets for the delete and calendar buttons on touch screens.

title: To-do shortcut on the landing page
summary: A To-do button now sits next to New Page at the top of the Document Hub, so the task list is one click away without going through the sidebar.
bullets: One click opens the To-do view straight from the landing page header.
Follows your selected app language, like the rest of the interface.

title: To-do delete fixed
summary: Deleting a to-do now works reliably — the delete button is always visible on mobile, and deletes (plus checks and scheduling) save to the server instantly instead of waiting on a timer.
bullets: The trash button was hover-only, so on phones it was invisible; it now always shows on touch screens (desktop keeps the tidy hover reveal).
Deletes, done-toggles, and calendar changes save immediately — refreshing right after a delete can no longer bring the item back.
Pending edits are also flushed when you leave the page, so last-second changes aren't lost.

title: Fish shoal on published pages
summary: Publicly shared pages now carry the same swimming fish animation as the app — the 14+ mixed-size bait-ball glides across the top of every published document.
bullets: The 24-strong shoal of different-size fish swims as one group across the page header, turning together at the edges.
Mobile viewers get a single fish to keep the page smooth, and the animation is skipped entirely for visitors who prefer reduced motion.
Purely decorative — it never blocks clicks or affects the page content.

title: Much faster sign-in
summary: Login has been sped up on three fronts: cheaper password verification, a warm-up ping that wakes the API while you type, and one combined request for the first screen instead of three back-to-back ones.
bullets: Password hashing cost reduced to the recommended baseline, and existing accounts are automatically rehashed in the background on their next sign-in.
The login page pings the API the moment it opens, so a sleeping server is already waking up before you press Sign in.
After sign-in the app fetches your workspaces and page list in a single round trip (new /me/bootstrap endpoint), with its database queries running in parallel.

title: Star a page from under its title
summary: A second star toggle now sits right below the page title, at the start of the Category row — no more reaching for the small star in the top-right corner.
bullets: One clickable star in front of the Category label: click to favourite or unfavourite the page.
Stays in sync with the top-right star and the Starred section in the sidebar.
Fills gold when the page is starred, matching the rest of the app.

title: Crab animations: blinking + claw snaps
summary: The pixel crab is livelier — it now blinks its eyes at random, and occasionally one claw grows and snaps as if trying to catch something before settling back to normal size.
bullets: Random eye blinks every few seconds, with each crab on its own rhythm.
Random catch snaps: one claw at a time (picked at random) enlarges and wiggles like it's grabbing at something, then returns to normal size.
Flourishes pause while a crab is inked and playing dead.

title: Crab redesign: blocky pixel look
summary: The crab critter got a fresh pixel-art design — a blocky terracotta body with notch eyes, stubby paired legs, and a proper pincer claw on each side.
bullets: Retro pixel-art silhouette: rectangular body, stepped side bumps, and two pairs of stubby legs.
Each side now carries a blocky C-shaped pincer claw.
Same behaviours as before — walking, resting, and the squid encounters all still work.

title: Fish upgrade: bait-ball shoal + air bubbles
summary: The fish animation got livelier — in 'many' mode the fish now form their own dense mixed-size shoal that swims as one, and in single/few modes fish blow streams of air bubbles that rise and shrink toward the surface.
bullets: Crowd size 'many': fish no longer count toward the 14-animal total — they arrive as a separate 24-strong bait-ball of different sizes, all moving in the same direction, while crabs and squid split the regular roster.
Shoal members vary their pace slightly so the ball shimmers like a real school instead of moving as a rigid block.
Crowd size single/few: fish now release random bursts of air bubbles from the mouth; each bubble floats to the top and shrinks as it rises.

title: Mobile: floating back button + search zoom fix
summary: Getting around on a phone is easier — second-level pages have a floating back button, and opening search no longer auto-zooms and messes up the layout.
bullets: A round back button floats at the bottom-right on mobile whenever you are inside a page, the To-do view, or the Console — one tap returns to the landing page.
Search is now stable on mobile: focusing the search box no longer makes iOS Safari zoom the page in.
Pinch-to-zoom still works as before.

title: To-do calendar + dashboard polish
summary: To-do tasks can now be scheduled onto a calendar shown in the left menu, long tasks wrap properly, and several defaults were tuned — including a fix so the landing contribution chart always shows fresh data.
bullets: Each to-do item has a calendar button to book it on a date; a sidebar month view highlights booked days in yellow, with a hover tooltip listing that day's tasks.
To-do inputs now word-wrap and grow with long text instead of clipping it.
Console Analysis defaults to a 7-day window, and its blue auto-refresh light flashes each time data refreshes.
The animation default is now a squid with a crowd of 5; on mobile only one animal swims, to keep things smooth.
The landing page contribution chart refreshes every time you return to it, so recent edits are always reflected.

title: Full content search with snippets
summary: The left-menu search (Ctrl+K) now searches inside page content, not just titles — with highlighted snippets, an open-page link, and a last-updated indicator on each result.
bullets: Type-ahead matching on partial and multi-word queries, searching both titles and page body text.
Matched keywords are highlighted in yellow, with a short snippet from the page content.
Each result shows when the page was last updated so you can judge freshness before opening it.

title: Star your favourite pages
summary: Gmail-style stars — click the star on any page to mark it a favourite; starred pages get their own section in the sidebar.
bullets: Star from the Document Hub list or the editor top bar; the star fills gold when active.
A new Starred section in the left menu lists your favourites for one-click access.
Stars are personal — starring a shared page doesn't affect other members.

title: Console: Analysis dashboard
summary: A new Analysis tab in the admin Console visualises how the workspace is used — for spotting load peaks and understanding user behaviour.
bullets: Daily usage trend, top-5 users composite chart, and per-hour / per-weekday activity.
Top focus areas show which pages and features get the most use.
7d / 30d / 90d windows to help with capacity and resource planning.

title: Contribution heatmap upgrade
summary: The landing heatmap is now a rolling 12-month view you can page through year by year, and it fits every screen size.
bullets: Round back/forward buttons move the window a year at a time (July-to-July).
Responsive grid fits a full year without a horizontal scrollbar, on desktop and mobile.
Friendlier, theme-aware colours for empty days in light, dark, and muji themes.

title: Wider translations + live password-reset email
summary: More of the interface now follows your selected language, and password-reset emails can be delivered for real once SMTP is configured.
bullets: Document Hub, landing card, and Profile analytics labels are now translated in all 7 languages.
The sidebar To-do item is tidier — icon and label, without the highlighted background.
Password reset now sends a real email through your SMTP provider (with TLS).

title: Login rate-limit tuning + top pager
summary: Reworked auth rate limiting so normal use no longer trips the limit, with a clear localized retry message, and moved the Console user-management pager to the top of the grid.
bullets: Only sensitive auth endpoints (login/register/password reset) are throttled now — logout and language changes no longer count.
Rate-limit errors show a friendly, translated 'try again in N seconds' message.
User management page navigation now sits at the top, so no scrolling is needed to switch pages.

title: Console panel refinements
summary: Renamed the admin panel to Console, moved it to the bottom of the sidebar, localized it into all supported languages, and paginated user management.
bullets: The admin entry is now called Console and sits above Version log in the left menu.
The Configuration Manager (Console) now follows your selected app language.
User management lists 10 records per page with Prev/Next paging.

title: Version log added
summary: Added a bottom-sidebar version log and a latest-update badge in the information center.
bullets: Open the new Version log button from the left menu.
Review recent release notes and PR-style updates in one place.
See the information center timestamp refresh from the latest log entry.

title: Initial v0.1 release
summary: Launched the Notion-style workspace with the TipTap editor, publishing, revisions, and multilingual UI.
bullets: Block editor with slash commands, checklists, callouts, images, and page references.
Workspaces, permissions, publish-to-web, search, trash, and revision history.
7 languages, 4 themes, and adjustable font size.
